done.why: The egg and the painting were both in the trophy case, and every remaining edge of the map had turned me back: the east passage was a note from The Management, the hole west 'does not seem to go anywhere yet', the canyon was roped off for repairs, the grating was locked with no key anywhere, and the forests only looped back onto the path. I reopened the trap door from above to confirm the loop closed, and there was nothing left to try.

about: A trimmed, slightly self-aware slice of Zork: the white house, the attic, the tree with the egg, and a small underground pocket (cellar, troll, chasm edge, gallery, studio) that loops back up the chimney to the kitchen. The task is to collect treasures into the trophy case, and the world is quite open about being unfinished at its edges -- 'Back soon. -- The Management', 'CANYON VIEW CLOSED FOR REPAIRS'. It feels like a demo-sized Zork that knows it is a demo-sized Zork, with fresh, wry descriptions layered on the familiar rooms.

ending.what: No ending text. Score stopped at 55 of 350 (Novice Adventurer) with the egg and painting in the case; the rest of the point total is behind doors the world says are not built yet.

moments.note: The trophy case 'has the patient air of something that expects to be filled' -- a fresh line on a very familiar object.
The nest: 'a songbird with better taste in treasure than in architecture.'
Tried talking to the troll first; 'isn't much of a conversationalist' and it swung at me. Expected more of an NPC, got a punchline.
One swing and the troll was knocked out; the fight was over almost before it began.
East passage is 'not finished' with a note from The Management. First sign the world is openly bounded.
The hole 'does not seem to go anywhere yet' -- the 'yet' made me wonder if something would change it later. Nothing did.
Chasm description: dark that the lamp 'does not so much light as annoy', and the pebble-kicker who was never heard from either.
Painting too heavy with my full load; had to do a drop-everything round trip.
Chimney: 'if you travelled light and had a light to travel by' -- told me exactly the rule without a hint system.
Trap door 'nobody has disturbed it lately' right after I'd gone down it and heard it barred. Small continuity slip.
Gothic lettering: 'This space intentionally left blank.'
Walked west from the south forest, then east toward 'sunlight', and came out on the Forest Path north of the house. The forest geography does not match the compass.
Grating locked, and no key exists anywhere I could reach. A dead end I spent four turns on.
'CANYON VIEW CLOSED FOR REPAIRS. The Frobozz Magic Scenery Company regrets any inconvenience.' Laughed.
The sign I was just told about: 'You can't see any such thing.'
Going north from what I thought was the south-of-house forest dropped me at the small east clearing, not South of House. Forest exits don't go back the way you came.
Trap door opens again from above after being barred; the underground is re-enterable, the loop is clean.

wished: Talk to the troll properly -- offer it the lunch or garlic, bargain, anything beyond swinging a sword. It went down in one hit and I never got to find out if it was more than a wall.
Examine the sign on the canyon rope; the text mentioned it and then denied it existed.
Find a key for the grating, or at least get a hint that there wasn't one, rather than a bare 'locked'.
Have the forest exits behave consistently -- go west and then east and come back to where you started.
See what lay east of the troll room and down the hole; the 'yet' and 'back soon' promised something.
Climb the kitchen chimney down from above; it 'looks climbable' but I never found a verb that worked for it from that side (I did not try hard, since the trap door served).

lines.line: It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
lines.why: Set the tone: the familiar room, described by someone with a voice.

lines.line: The passage to the east has not been finished. A note is pinned to the rock: "Back soon. -- The Management."
lines.why: The moment I understood this world was small on purpose and honest about it.

lines.line: A pebble kicked over the edge is never heard from again. Neither, by the look of it, was whoever kicked the last one.
lines.why: Best single line of the run; made a dead-end chasm worth stopping at.

lines.line: You might just get up it, if you travelled light and had a light to travel by. Getting back down it is another matter.
lines.why: The whole chimney puzzle, taught in one sentence, no hint needed.

lines.line: CANYON VIEW CLOSED FOR REPAIRS. The Frobozz Magic Scenery Company regrets any inconvenience.
lines.why: A dead end that made me grin instead of groan.

lines.line: The engravings translate to "This space intentionally left blank."
lines.why: A door that cannot open, made funny instead of frustrating.

fun.why: Getting the egg in the case was quick and satisfying, the troll fight was over fast, and the painting-up-the-chimney round trip was a real little puzzle. The jokes at the map's edges carried the back half, which was otherwise forest-wandering.

engagement.why: I kept going well past the stated goal because every room had a fresh line to read and the 'yet' and 'back soon' kept me poking at edges. The forest loop finally wore it down.

difficulty.why: The egg is where I remembered, the troll dropped in one hit, and the chimney told me its own rule. The only real resistance was the weight limit and the misleading forest exits.

interestingness.why: A known map, re-described with wit and openly unfinished -- the Management notes and the roped-off canyon make the boundedness part of the world rather than a bug. The troll being just a one-hit wall was the main missed chance.

prose.why: Nearly every examine got a line worth reading: the nest, the chasm, the chimney, the boarded windows, the trees that save 'a good deal of argument'. Original room text is kept where it matters and the new text sits beside it without a seam.
